class.name: NetwDisplay
class.brief_description: How one [NetwEntity] is drawn, reached by [member NetwEntity.display].
class.description: A [NetwInterpolate] configures one property. This handle holds the settings that apply to the whole entity, such as which node receives the smoothed values and how far behind the newest snapshot it is drawn. [codeblock] var handle := NetwEntity.of(self).display handle.visual_root = NodePath("Visual") handle.display_role = DISPLAY_ROLE_REMOTE [/codeblock] Settings written before the entity is spawned are applied once it is, and they are kept if the entity respawns.

method.name: displayed_authoring_tick
method.description: The tick the drawn state was written at, or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: entity
method.description: The [NetwEntity] this handle belongs to, or [code]null[/code] once that entity is gone.

method.name: get_track_stat
method.description: Returns the display diagnostic [param stat] of [param property], or [code]null[/code] for an unknown stat. An empty [param property] reads the whole entity.

method.name: reset
method.description: Clears the entity's interpolation history and writes its current values to the visual. Call it after teleporting the entity locally, so it does not interpolate from the old position.

members.member: Seconds [constant LIVE_MODE_CHASE] takes to smooth out a correction.
The extra display delay in ticks that [member enable_smart_dilation] has added.
How this entity is drawn. [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTO] picks one from [member NetwSimulation.mode] and who controls the entity, and is right for most entities.
Lets the display delay of a remote entity grow when snapshots arrive late.
How quickly, as a fraction per frame, the smallest delay [member enable_smart_dilation] measures follows a new measurement. Lower is smoother.
How quickly, as a fraction per frame, [member display_lag] shrinks back toward the smallest delay needed once snapshots arrive on time.
How an entity this peer simulates is drawn under [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_PREDICTED], in [constant NetwSimulation.MODE_PREDICT] or [constant NetwSimulation.MODE_ACTIVE].
Smoothing time in seconds for [constant LIVE_MODE_CHASE]. [code]0[/code] uses one tick.
The most ticks [member display_lag] may grow to.
How many ticks [constant TIMELINE_MODE_FORECAST] may guess ahead before it stops.
How this entity is being interpolated right now, or [constant DISPLAY_PUMP_UNRESOLVED] before that is decided.
How many frames without a new snapshot are tolerated before [member display_lag] starts growing.
Ticks added to [member display_lag] per frame once the grace frames are spent.
How a remote entity is displayed.
Frames between interpolation trace logs. [code]0[/code] disables them.

The child node that receives the smoothed values. Position and rotation are written in global space, and other properties are written as they are. A visual with [member CanvasItem.top_level] set receives every property in global space.

constants.constant: Picked from [member NetwSimulation.mode]. The default. Predicted entities use [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_PREDICTED], received ones [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_REMOTE], ones this peer controls without prediction [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_DISABLED], and the server uses [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTHORITY].
Interpolate between received states. Used for other players' entities.
Follow the locally predicted body, as set by [member NetwDisplay.live_mode]. Used for the player's own entity.
No smoothing. The game moves the node itself.
Record the server's own simulation every tick and interpolate it, so the host sees it as smooth as clients do.
Interpolate received states, as with [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_REMOTE].
Interpolate between the previous and current tick, one tick behind. Used by [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTHORITY] and [constant LIVE_MODE_BRACKETED].
Move the visual toward the body every frame. Used by [constant LIVE_MODE_CHASE].
Move the visual toward the body every frame. Most responsive, but corrections are visible.
Interpolate between the previous and current tick. Smoother, and one tick behind.
Display slightly in the past, between received states. The default, and always used on the server.
Guess ahead from the last received velocity. Less delay, but it ignores collisions, so a body can move into a wall until the next update arrives.
